sections.title: Form and texture
sections.text: Spongiforma squarepantsii Desjardin, Peay & T.D. Bruns forms a small, solitary fruitbody on the ground. It is irregularly globose to ovoid, brain-like and spongy, about 3–5 cm across and 2–3 cm tall, with a pliant, rubbery texture. It has no stem, distinct cap or outer skin; the external sterile ridges are whitish to pale orange.

sections.title: Locules and fertile surface
sections.text: Branching folds delimit irregular labyrinthine cavities (locules), generally 2–10 mm wide. The orange to deep-orange hymenium lines their inner walls, while pale sterile ridges divide them. A longitudinal cut may reveal a narrow, branched white central columella connected to a white rhizomorph. This is a gasteroid bolete: its internal cavities are neither gills nor tubes beneath a cap.

sections.title: Habitat and biology
sections.text: The species is known from tropical rainforest in Lambir Hills National Park, Sarawak, northern Borneo, Malaysia, where it was collected on the ground beneath undetermined dipterocarp trees. It occurs in forest dominated by these ectomycorrhizal trees; an ectomycorrhizal association is probable, but the authors say it still needs confirmation by observing colonized roots. It should therefore not be described as an established saprotroph.

sections.title: Odour and taxonomic caution
sections.text: The reported odour ranges from vaguely fruity to strongly musty, not coal-tar-like. This combination of shape, orange interior and odour helps distinguish it from Spongiforma thailandica, known from Thailand and described as grey-brown to reddish-brown with a coal-tar odour. Published records of S. squarepantsii remain very restricted; visual resemblance alone cannot identify a specimen. Food status is not assessed here.

traits: Small, solitary, irregularly globose to ovoid, brain-like and rubbery fruitbody; no stem or cap
Whitish to pale-orange sterile outer ridges; orange to deep-orange fertile tissue lines internal labyrinthine locules 2–10 mm wide
A longitudinal cut may show a narrow, branched white columella; no gills or tubes
On the ground beneath dipterocarps in tropical rainforest at Lambir Hills, Sarawak, Borneo
Probable but unconfirmed ectomycorrhizal association; fruity to musty odour, not coal tar
safetyNote: Taxonomic and ecological reference, not an identification guide or food-safety assessment. The species' biology remains poorly documented and records are rare. Do not identify or eat a mushroom based only on this page or a photograph.
